newsitem.title: UK: BOXING-FORMER CHAMP EUBANK GUILTY OF FIREWORKS HORROR.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-FORMER CHAMP EUBANK GUILTY OF FIREWORKS HORROR.

text.p: British former world champion boxer Chris Eubank was on Friday sentenced to 200 hours community service for staging an unofficial fireworks display which went badly wrong and left two women scarred for life.

"I was foolish and I am deeply ashamed of my conduct. I am deeply sorry for what has happened," said Eubank, a former holder of the World Boxing Organisation (WBO) middleweight and super middleweight titles.
He had pleaded guilty to two charges of causing grievous bodily harm on December 31, 1995 during a fireworks display in the southern resort of Brighton.

Stray sparks from the display set off fireworks in nearby plastic bags which shot across the beach and hit two women passers-by in the back, setting fire to their clothing. Both victims spent five days in a specialist burns unit.
Eubank, who retired in 1995 but began a comeback a year later, was also told to pay 1,100 pounds ($1,800) costs. The two women are suing him for damages.
